title: South Korea's Education Minister Quits After Exam Cheating Scandal
summary:
South Korea's education minister has quit after a cheating scandal shook one of the country's most important exams. Choi Kyo-jin said on Sunday that he took full responsibility for the confusion caused by steps to stop cheating with artificial intelligence during Thursday's entrance exam, known as the Suneung. About 500,000 students took the exam this year, and it can take up to nine hours.

The trouble began earlier, when the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted he had cheated. Han Won-seok, 34, said he had used a tiny camera to photograph the questions and send them to an AI tool, then checked his answers on his smartphone. He had gotten just one out of 160 questions wrong.

With only days to go, officials rushed to add checks for hidden devices. They sent three emergency alerts to every mobile phone between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. on Thursday, making phones blare even on silent mode.

The measures left honest test takers nervous, and 111 candidates were found with unauthorized smart devices. President Lee Jae Myung accepted Choi's resignation.
why_it_matters: It matters because fair tests matter to you too, since cheating and confusing rules can hurt honest students who worked hard.

Artificial intelligence is a computer system that can learn and answer questions like a person.

Unauthorized means not allowed by the rules.
A resignation is when someone chooses to leave their job.
